questions.q: How much cash (and other assets) does the inheritance include?
questions.why: Drives estate-tax exposure, investment paths, and whether the house decision even matters financially.
questions.how: Executor's preliminary inventory; no personal figures enter this site.

questions.q: Will the decedent's estate exceed the federal exclusion (projected ~$15M+ indexed) in the year of death?
questions.why: 40% federal tax above the exclusion is paid by the estate before distribution.
questions.status: PARTIAL — 2026 rules verified; year-of-death exclusion unknown
questions.how: Attorney's estate projection; ask about portability election and prior taxable gifts (Form 709 history).

questions.q: Are there prior taxable lifetime gifts?
questions.why: Reduces the available basic exclusion (anti-clawback protects prior use at the higher exemption).
questions.how: Ask executor/counsel for gift-tax returns filed since 1977.

questions.q: Will the heir occupy Property A as a principal residence long-term (and file within 1 year)?
questions.why: This single fact decides Prop 19 treatment: occupancy keeps a capped base; non-occupancy triggers full reassessment at FMV.
questions.how: Household agreement in writing before transfer (see Suggestions).

questions.q: What is Property A's tax rate area (TRA) number, and what rate does the county publish for it?
questions.why: All property-tax projections hinge on the actual all-in TRA rate (household bill implies ~1.34%).
questions.how: Read TRA off any prior tax bill; look up in county tax rate book.

questions.q: Why does Property B's bill imply ~2.14% when the official SF base rate is 1.18162%?
questions.why: Direct levies/parcel taxes explain part of the gap; errors are possible.
questions.how: Request parcel breakdown from SF Treasurer; compare to published direct-levy schedule.

questions.q: What is the actual insurance premium (Property A and B) — and is Property B insured as a rental (DP-3/LL policy)?
questions.why: Household estimates (~$1,500) sit below CA DOI statewide averages; underinsurance is a tail risk.
questions.how: Two broker quotes each; also pull ZIP-level CDI report figures for both property ZIPs (internal).

questions.q: What rent will Property A actually command?
questions.why: Rent path ranking is a floor until real comparables exist; HUD FMR is a voucher benchmark only.
questions.how: Three licensed-comp appraisals/BPOs or a property-manager rent analysis.

questions.q: Are Property B's leases written, assigned to the trust/heir, and compliant with SF Rent Ordinance registration?
questions.why: Lease terms, rent-control status and just-cause rules determine B's income durability.
questions.how: Produce all leases, registration certificates, and any banked-rent history.

questions.q: Is Property A free of debt? Any liens?
questions.why: Debt must be repaid or assumed at transfer; changes every net-worth figure.

questions.q: Is Property A on NEM 1.0/2.0 (grandfathered) or NEM 3.0?
questions.why: Solar economics differ ~5x on export credits; affects the +$10–$20/mo credit assumption.

questions.q: Does the household prefer liquidity, income, or appreciation — and what drawdown is unacceptable?
questions.why: Pre-agreed preferences prevent reverse-engineering the answer from one projection.
questions.how: Sign the pre-commitment policy on the Suggestions page.

questions.q: Could the estate need §6166 installment payments or life-insurance liquidity?
questions.why: Estate tax is due in 9 months in cash — illiquid real estate cannot pay it alone.
questions.how: Estate liquidity plan with counsel (briefing sheet lists the questions).

questions.q: Are there out-of-state heirs or property with ancillary-probate implications?
questions.why: Changes timelines and possibly state estate taxes (CA itself imposes none).
questions.how: Ask counsel about situs of assets and heir residences.

front.changes: If liquid assets ≫ house value, the house decision shrinks; if the estate approaches the federal exclusion, estate tax and liquidity planning dominate every other choice.

front.lever: Will you occupy Property A long-term?
front.changes: Occupancy + filing within 1 year preserves a capped Prop 19 base (saves roughly the cap amount × tax rate each year, ~$20k+/yr at 2045 values); not occupying triggers full FMV reassessment.

front.lever: Real market rent for Property A
front.changes: If comps come in well above the floor, RENT path climbs; if below, SELL/LIVE strengthen.

front.lever: Where markets start when the house is sold
front.changes: A 1929-style entry destroys lump-sum proceeds; a V-shaped crash (2008) punishes slow phasing. This is why the phased-Treasury path exists.

front.lever: Occupancy intent vs. SF rent control
front.changes: If B's leases end or rules tighten, LIVE-in-A becomes relatively more attractive (B income falls).
The cap re-adjusts each Feb 16; a higher cap at 2040s transfer dates widens the occupancy advantage.
CA 60+ exemption initiative (targeted 2028), federal estate-rate bills, or new SF transfer-tax measures could move the numbers materially.
